summary: The round-4 major is fixed in the geometry. I re-rendered the LRS-100 datasheet page 4 and measured it: SVR1 at x 4.7, y 9.7 and the LED at x 11.0, y 10.0, which matches the catalog's 5.1/9.6 and 11.1/9.9. psu_hood cuts an 8 mm hole and a 3.5 mm hole at those points, in the solid top (x 0-20), referenced to the -Y wall that bears on the case's y = 0 face. The 5.4 V trim (WIRING step 21, DESIGN step 11) can now be set and checked at the WAGO bus with the hood closed and no mains terminal exposed. The side vent window (x 13-27, z 2-12) covers the datasheet's slots, which measure x 15.7-25.7, z 3-9 (round 4's z 9-13 was a misreading). The tie bridge replaces the floor slots, the cable_mast docstring is correct, and at 5.4 V the worst stall row is 4.951 V against 4.8 V. The arm geometry has not changed since round 4. Poses, FEA hot spots and load cases are still consistent. Only minor items remain.

findings.issue: The SVR hole (d 8 at x 5.1, y 9.6) and the LED hole (d 3.5 at x 11.1, y 9.9) are 6.0 mm apart centre to centre. That leaves a 0.26 mm web between them (6.007 - 4 - 1.75), less than one 0.4 mm extrusion line. It will print as a ragged sliver or not at all, and the two holes merge into one 8 x 12 mm slot. This is still finger-safe (8 mm wide is less than the 12 mm IEC test finger) and the mains pins are 50 mm or more away, so it is cosmetic and robustness only.
findings.fix: Leave at least 1.2 mm web: cut the LED hole at 2.5 mm, or move it to x 12 (the LED still shows, given the ±1 mm case tolerance). Alternatively, cut one deliberate rounded slot over both.

findings.issue: The assembly order (project.yaml assembly_note, ASSEMBLY step 26) says to slide the hood on, feed the DC pairs out, then 'tie them to the floor bridge'. Once the hood is seated, the bridge (x -12, y -43.5..-37.5, z 2-7) is enclosed: the top covers x -65..20, the inlet fills the end window, and the only opening near it is the 10 mm DC exit 5 mm away. You cannot thread a tie through the X-direction tunnel through that hole. Separately, in the print orientation (standing on the end wall) the bridge block's -X face is a 6 x 5 mm flat overhang that sticks out 5 mm from a vertical wall. Report overhang is only 0.23 %, so it will just sag a little.
findings.fix: Reword the note: feed the DC pairs out of the exit and tie them to the bridge with the hood held beside the supply, then lower or slide the hood on and fit the side screw. Optionally, chamfer the bridge block's -X underside at 45 degrees.

findings.issue: Carried over, now with more margin. The IR-drop rows still leave out the 5 A ATO fuse's catalog cold_resistance_ohm (0.01785 ohm, about 45 mV at 2.5 A), the fuse holder's 16 AWG lead, and the plug-to-extension contacts. They also assume the servo's own lead is 22 AWG, but no gauge is sourced. At 5.4 V the wrist and grip stall rows are 4.951 V, 151 mV above 4.8 V, so the omitted terms (roughly 60-110 mV) still leave positive margin. kerf/electrical.py was not changed.
findings.fix: Engine: add the fuse's cold resistance and the holder lead to the run's loop resistance (the data is already in the catalog), and add a sourced lead gauge to the servo catalog entries.

findings.issue: The docstring is now correct (the column is centred on the 26 mm foot and printed lying down on support). The 12.6 % support surface remains, so the support side of the column will be rough. This is cosmetic.
findings.fix: Optional: shift the column flush with one long side of the foot so it lies on the bed with no support.

findings.issue: Carried over and accepted: the Nano, the 4 WAGO splices and the 5 inline fuse holders sit loose on the desk behind the base. DESIGN.md tells the builder to case the Nano and screw the supply down. The supply's plan M3 holes take a screw only 3 mm deep.
findings.fix: None required. A printed electronics tray on the rear pad would make the layout tidy and short-proof.

findings.issue: Accepted, for the record. yoke_r_fea peaks at 17.7 MPa and upper_arm_stall at 18.8 MPa, both local singularities. Their p99.9 values (6.55 against 13 and 13.42 against 24 MPa) pass. The hot spots in the renders are on the load path (the cheek root at the foot, and the frame of the servo window in plate A). The DS32xx tab holes are still UNVERIFIED in the catalog.
findings.fix: None required. Test-print yoke_r and fit a real DS3225 before printing the rest, as the Risks section of DESIGN.md says.
